jurisdictions.classification: Financial derivative (Swap) — event contracts are "swaps" under the CEA
jurisdictions.regulatory_body: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission)
jurisdictions.licensing_framework: Designated Contract Market (DCM) under CEA Section 5
jurisdictions.key_legislation: Commodity Exchange Act (CEA); Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act (2010) — CEA § 5c(c)(5)(C) defines prohibited event contracts (TAWGA)
jurisdictions.pending_bills: Event Contract Enforcement Act (Moore-Carbajal, 2026-03-06); End Prediction Market Corruption Act (S. 4017, Merkley, 2026-03-05); Public Integrity in Financial Prediction Markets Act (H.R. 7004, 2026); Prediction Markets Security and Integrity Act (Blumenthal-Kim, 2026); Fair Markets and Sports Integrity Act (H.R. 7477); Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act (2026)
jurisdictions.federal_preemption: Asserted by CFTC; CEA preemption of state gambling laws claimed under exclusive jurisdiction; split in courts (upheld in NJ; reversed in NV Dec 2025; rejected in MA/MD/OH); CFTC filed amicus in 9th Circuit
jurisdictions.tax_treatment: Section 1256 contracts (60% long-term / 40% short-term capital gains) for CFTC-regulated event contracts; H.R. 4304 (FAIR Bet Tax Act) pending
jurisdictions.insider_trading_rules: No existing federal insider trading law for event contracts; Prediction Markets Security and Integrity Act (Blumenthal-Kim) would prohibit MNPI-based trading; platforms added voluntary rules

polymarket.status: Active (returned to US as DCM via QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US, Nov 2025); previously settled $1.4M penalty in 2022

robinhood.status: Active (event contracts since March 2025); Rothera JV with Susquehanna acquiring MIAXdx (closed 2026-01-20)

cme.status: Active (event contracts launched via FanDuel Predicts, Dec 2025; 100M+ contracts in 8 weeks)

cboe.status: Pending (patent-pending 3-outcome framework announced 2026-03-09; Mini-SPX contract planned Q2 2026)

nasdaq.status: Pending (filed with SEC for binary options on Nasdaq-100, 2026-03-02)

source.description: SEC Release No. 34-104966, File No. SR-MRX-2026-05

markets.political: Allowed — D.C. court ruled Congressional Control Contracts not "gaming" in Kalshi v. CFTC; CFTC dropped appeal May 2025
markets.sports: Allowed federally; contested by states — ~90% of Kalshi volume is sports; 19+ federal lawsuits by states
markets.death_terrorism: Prohibited under CEA § 5c(c)(5)(C) (TAWGA); Event Contract Enforcement Act would mandate CFTC enforcement

jurisdictions.summary: CFTC asserts exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts as swaps under the CEA. Chairman Selig withdrew Biden-era ban (Feb 2026), opened ANPRM (Mar 2026), and filed amicus briefs defending federal preemption. Sports contracts face aggressive state pushback via 19+ lawsuits. Circuit split on federal preemption (upheld in NJ; reversed in NV; rejected in MA/MD/OH). 6+ Congressional bills target insider trading, prohibited contract types, and state authority. Fed FEDS paper validated PM forecasting quality. CME, Cboe, Nasdaq, Robinhood entering alongside Kalshi and Polymarket.

jurisdictions.summary: Hawaii — where all gambling is already prohibited — advancing HB 2198 to explicitly include prediction markets in gambling definition. Passed House, would take effect July 1, 2026. Would be first US state to enact explicit PM ban. Covers sports, political, disaster, and death-related contracts.

States with existing sports betting frameworks may assert jurisdiction as the federal-state conflict develops.

jurisdictions.summary: No unified EU prediction market framework exists. MiCA regulates crypto infrastructure but does not address PMs directly. Grandfathering for existing crypto operators ends July 1, 2026. Country-by-country bans are accumulating faster than any framework. France, Belgium, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Hungary, Romania, Italy have all banned or restricted Polymarket. Germany and Spain remain accessible. Eurex reportedly evaluating entry.

battlegrounds.name: Federal Preemption vs. State Authority
battlegrounds.core_tension: Does the CEA give the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts, or can states regulate PMs under gambling law?
battlegrounds.side_a: **Pro-preemption:** CFTC (Chairman Selig), Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood, Coalition for PMs. Argue CEA grants exclusive federal jurisdiction over event contracts as swaps/derivatives. CFTC filed amicus in 9th Circuit.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Anti-preemption:** 38 state AGs (amicus supporting MD), state gaming commissions, sportsbook lobby, Mick Mulvaney / "Gambling Is Not Investing." Argue states retain regulatory authority over gambling regardless of federal derivative classification.
battlegrounds.key_cases: Kalshi v. CFTC (D.C., won on election contracts) [KalshiEX LLC v. CFTC, No. 24-5205 (D.C. Cir.)](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/cadc/24-5205/24-5205-2024-10-02.html) (2024-10-02); Kalshi v. NJ (won, preemption upheld, 3d Cir. appeal); Kalshi v. MD (lost, 4th Cir. appeal); MA v. Kalshi (injunction granted 2026-01-20); NV dissolved injunction Dec 2025; CFTC amicus in 9th Circuit [CFTC PR 9183-26](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9183-26) (2026-02-17)
battlegrounds.current_status: Circuit split. 19+ federal lawsuits across multiple circuits. Pro-preemption win in NJ (on appeal to 3d Cir.); anti-preemption wins in MA/MD/NV(reversed Nov 2025)/OH. CT issued C&D orders but Kalshi won temporary relief. 36-38 state AGs filed amicus briefs supporting state authority in multiple circuits. CFTC actively intervening via amicus briefs.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Heading to appellate courts and likely Supreme Court within 12-24 months. Congress may legislate first via PM Security and Integrity Act (which would reverse preemption) or CFTC ANPRM process.
battlegrounds.industry_impact: Platforms cannot operate nationally without resolution. State-by-state compliance is prohibitively expensive. New entrants frozen until jurisdictional question settled.
battlegrounds.resolution_scenarios: (1) Supreme Court rules on preemption — 2+ years. (2) Congress passes explicit federal framework via CFTC ANPRM. (3) PM Security and Integrity Act reverses preemption. (4) Fragmented state-by-state regime persists.

battlegrounds.name: Gambling vs. Derivatives Classification
battlegrounds.core_tension: Are prediction markets gambling or financial derivatives? Classification determines regulator, rules, tax treatment, and legitimacy.
battlegrounds.side_a: **Derivatives:** CFTC, Kalshi, exchanges (CME, Cboe). Event contracts are swaps under CEA. Used for hedging and price discovery. Fed FEDS paper validated forecasting quality.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Gambling:** State AGs, sportsbook operators, Mulvaney. Sports contracts are "indistinguishable" from wagers (MD ruling). 90% of volume is sports. "If it looks like a sports bet..."
battlegrounds.key_cases: MD ruling: sports contracts = wagering; NV ruling: parlays/props not swaps; D.C.: election contracts not "gaming"; NJ: event contracts are swaps
battlegrounds.current_status: No consensus. Different courts reaching different conclusions on same question. CFTC ANPRM seeks to establish clear federal framework. Classification varies by contract type (sports vs. economic vs. political).
battlegrounds.trajectory: Sports contracts most likely to be classified as gambling; economic/political contracts more likely to survive as derivatives. Bifurcated framework emerging.
battlegrounds.industry_impact: Classification determines who regulates (CFTC vs. state gaming), what license needed, tax rate, age requirements, and consumer protections.

battlegrounds.name: Sports Betting Overlap
battlegrounds.core_tension: PMs are siphoning $600M+ in state sports betting tax revenue. States argue sports event contracts are unlicensed sports bets.
battlegrounds.side_a: **Pro-PM sports:** Kalshi (90% sports volume), Polymarket. Argue sports contracts are derivatives not bets. Point to federal DCM authorization.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Anti-PM sports:** State AGs, licensed sportsbooks (DraftKings, FanDuel), AGA. $600M+ lost tax revenue. 11 states issued cease-and-desist orders. Licensed operators paying 15-20% tax while PMs pay zero.
battlegrounds.current_status: Most active battleground. 11 states issued C&D orders. Kalshi took $1.9B in college basketball wagers in Feb 2026 alone. KY HB 904 bans sportsbook-PM partnerships. Moore-Carbajal bill would give states opt-out on sports contracts.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Sports contracts face highest regulatory risk. Even pro-PM lawmakers (Moore) support state authority over sports. Likely outcome: sports PMs either banned, taxed at parity with sportsbooks, or subject to state opt-in.
battlegrounds.industry_impact: Sports is 87-90% of Kalshi and 38% of Polymarket volume. Losing sports contracts would devastate PM revenue models.

battlegrounds.name: Insider Trading & National Security
battlegrounds.core_tension: Can people profit from classified information via PMs? Should PMs on war, terrorism, and death exist? Bipartisan concern.
battlegrounds.side_a: **Pro-regulation:** Bipartisan Congress (Moore, Merkley, Blumenthal, Schiff), state AGs, Governor Newsom. Iran strikes scandal proved the risk.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Self-regulation sufficient:** Kalshi (200 investigations, 2 referrals), Polymarket (Palantir surveillance partnership). Voluntary rules already in place.
battlegrounds.key_cases: Iran strikes ($515K suspicious trade, Feb 2026); Maduro ouster ($400K+ suspicious trade, Jan 2026); Israeli arrests of insiders
battlegrounds.current_status: 3+ Congressional bills targeting insider trading (S. 4017, H.R. 7004, PM Security Act). CA Governor signed EO. No existing federal insider trading law for event contracts.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Insider trading legislation most likely to pass — bipartisan support. Question is scope: narrow (officials only) vs. broad (all MNPI).
battlegrounds.industry_impact: If broad insider trading rules pass, could affect market liquidity and discourage informed trading (the mechanism that makes PMs valuable).

battlegrounds.name: Market Listing Standards & Repugnance
battlegrounds.core_tension: What should and shouldn't be a prediction market? Who decides? Death/terrorism/assassination markets create moral hazard and perverse incentives.
battlegrounds.side_a: **Restrict:** Moore-Carbajal Event Contract Enforcement Act requires CFTC to prohibit TAWGA contracts (terrorism, assassination, war, gaming, illegal activity) + elections + government activity.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Allow with guardrails:** CFTC ANPRM exploring which contracts may be "contrary to public interest" vs. allowed. Self-regulation approach.
battlegrounds.current_status: CEA § 5c(c)(5)(C) already lists TAWGA categories but CFTC not required to enforce. Moore-Carbajal would mandate enforcement and add elections/government activity.
battlegrounds.trajectory: TAWGA enforcement mandate likely to pass. Election/government contracts more contested — some argue they serve legitimate informational purpose.

battlegrounds.name: Self-Regulation vs. Mandated Oversight
battlegrounds.core_tension: Are platform voluntary rules sufficient, or does Congress need to mandate specific oversight?
battlegrounds.side_a: **Self-regulation:** Kalshi (200 investigations, 2 referrals), Polymarket (Palantir partnership). DCMs already self-regulatory organizations supervised by CFTC.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Mandated oversight:** Congress (PM Security Act), bipartisan senators. Self-regulation insufficient — Iran/Maduro scandals occurred despite voluntary rules.
battlegrounds.current_status: CFTC staff advisory (9193-26) reminded DCMs of existing regulatory obligations. ANPRM exploring enhanced oversight.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Enhanced mandatory oversight likely — question is whether via CFTC rulemaking or Congressional legislation.

battlegrounds.name: Crypto Infrastructure & Regulatory Arbitrage
battlegrounds.core_tension: Polymarket runs on Polygon blockchain. MiCA constrains crypto infrastructure in EU without addressing PMs. Offshore platforms evade national regulation.
battlegrounds.side_a: **Crypto-native:** Polymarket. Decentralized infrastructure enables global access. Users bypass national bans via VPN.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Regulators:** EU (MiCA CASP deadline July 2026), national gambling regulators blocking access. India using DPI to block smart contract endpoints.
battlegrounds.current_status: MiCA grandfathering ends July 2026. 8+ EU countries banned Polymarket. India blocking at DPI level. Taiwan prosecuted users. Gap between regulation on paper and in practice.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Technical enforcement growing more sophisticated (DPI, smart contract blocking). MiCA deadline will force platforms to either get licensed or exit EU.

battlegrounds.name: Cross-Border Enforcement
battlegrounds.core_tension: A user in France trades on Polymarket (Polygon chain, no KYC for non-US). France bans it. Can they actually enforce?
battlegrounds.side_a: **Enforceable:** ISP blocks (SG, AU, TW, AR), DPI (India), app store restrictions, prosecution of users (TW — 17 arrested).
battlegrounds.side_b: **Unenforceable in practice:** VPN bypass widespread (India remains top user base despite ban), decentralized infrastructure, no KYC for non-US users.
battlegrounds.current_status: 30+ countries restrict Polymarket. Enforcement ranges from ISP blocks (most common) to user prosecution (Taiwan) to DPI (India). VPN usage persists everywhere.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Increasingly aggressive enforcement tools. But fundamental tension between decentralized crypto infrastructure and national jurisdiction remains unresolved.

battlegrounds.name: Consumer Protection & Market Integrity
battlegrounds.core_tension: What protections do PM users need? Wash trading, manipulation, addiction, KYC/AML, age verification, loss limits.
battlegrounds.side_a: **More protection:** MA AG (age 18 vs. 21 gambling age), Argentina (no age verification), state regulators. Sports betting has extensive consumer protections PMs lack.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Existing protections sufficient:** DCMs already regulated under CEA Part 38, DCM Core Principles. CFTC staff advisory emphasized existing obligations.
battlegrounds.current_status: CFTC staff advisory 9193-26 reminded DCMs of obligations. Argentina cited lack of age/identity verification. MA highlighted age gap (18 vs. 21).

battlegrounds.name: Traditional Exchange Entry & Institutional Legitimacy
battlegrounds.core_tension: CME, Cboe, Nasdaq, ICE entering PMs. Their participation transforms PMs from "crypto gambling" to "financial infrastructure."
battlegrounds.side_a: **Legitimizing:** CME-FanDuel launch, Cboe 3-outcome framework, Nasdaq SEC filing, Robinhood exchange acquisition, ICE $2B Polymarket investment. Fed FEDS paper validation.
battlegrounds.side_b: **Regulatory complexity:** Nasdaq filing went to SEC (not CFTC) — potential jurisdictional conflict. Cboe product as securities vs. CFTC derivatives.
battlegrounds.current_status: CME launched Dec 2025. Cboe Q2 2026. Nasdaq pending SEC approval. Robinhood acquired MIAXdx Jan 2026. FIA Boca — Kalshi CEO alongside CME/Nasdaq/Deutsche Börse CEOs.
battlegrounds.trajectory: Traditional exchange entry accelerating rapidly. Creates two-track system: exchange-traded PMs (heavily regulated, institutional) vs. crypto-native PMs (lighter regulation, retail).
